c.tagline: Taiwan's sunny harbor city of night markets, art piers, and island ferries.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are plentiful, metered and cheap; Uber and the local yoxi app both operate and let you pay by card, but street taxis usually want cash.

emergency.note: 119 reaches fire and ambulance; 110 is police. English may be limited, so ask a local to help if possible.

hood_landmark.Zuoying: Lotus Pond Dragon and Tiger Pagodas, Kaohsiung

hood_desc: The city's atmospheric old harbor quarter, home to the sprawling Pier-2 Art Center in converted warehouses, the Love River waterfront, and the Yancheng night market; a walkable, arty base close to the light rail and harbor ferries.

The central district around Kaohsiung Main Station and the buzzing Liuhe and Ruifeng night markets, sitting on the metro's Red and Orange line crossing; the most convenient, transit-connected place for first-timers to stay.

Kaohsiung's modern downtown of high-rise hotels, the 85 Sky Tower, the giant Dream Mall, and the Central Park nightlife and dining scene; best for travelers who want shopping, restaurants and bars on the doorstep.

The northern district wrapped around scenic Lotus Pond with its Dragon and Tiger Pagodas, Confucius Temple and Spring and Autumn Pavilions, and the high-speed rail gateway station; a sightseeing base with temples and a lake promenade.

The hilly bayside neighborhood by Sizihwan Bay and National Sun Yat-sen University, with the historic former British Consulate, Shoushan trails, sunset views and the little ferry across to Cijin Island; a relaxed, scenic corner of the city.
lodging: Kindness Hotel - Sanduo Shopping District Branch

water.note: Tap water is treated but locals boil or filter it; bottled water is everywhere.

transit.hours: The KMRT metro runs from around 6:00 AM to midnight; the Circular light rail and city buses run on similar daytime-to-late-evening hours.
transit.note: Kaohsiung has a clean, easy metro (KMRT) with two lines, the Red and the Orange, crossing at Formosa Boulevard, supplemented by the ground-level Circular Light Rail loop, an extensive city bus network, and cross-harbor ferries to Cijin.
transit.pay: Tap in and out with an EasyCard or iPASS stored-value card (buy and top up at stations and convenience stores); single-journey tokens are also sold at machines, and the same cards work on the light rail, buses and ferries.

bus: Intercity coaches (Kuo-Kuang, UBus) to Tainan, Taichung and Taipei

transit.m: KMRT Red Line from Kaohsiung International Airport station to city center (~15-20 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Taiwan; a 10% service charge is often added at hotels and higher-end restaurants, so no extra is expected.

food.name: Milkfish congee
food.desc: Southern Taiwan's signature fish, simmered into a clear rice porridge with the prized fatty belly and served mostly at breakfast.

places.name: Lao Cai Milkfish Congee
places.note: Long-running favourite for clear, clean porridge and a wall of side dishes.

places.name: Dagouding Milkfish Noodles
places.note: Decades-old stall doing milkfish in soup, noodles and congee.

places.name: Liuhe Night Market
places.note: Several stalls sell milkfish soup and seafood porridge late into the night.

food.name: Fish thick soup
food.desc: Yu geng: chunks of marlin or mackerel in a starch-thickened, slightly sweet-sour broth, a port-city staple eaten with black vinegar.

places.name: Liuhe Night Market
places.note: Fried fish thick soup and mackerel soup are among its best-known stalls.

places.name: Ziqiang Night Market
places.note: Small, locals-first market where the seafood stalls turn over fast.

places.name: Yancheng District old shops
places.note: The old harbour quarter is the traditional home of fish soup counters.

food.name: Beef noodle soup
food.desc: Braised beef shin and tendon in a dark, spiced broth over hand-pulled noodles, a dish Kaohsiung claims a founding role in.

places.name: Gang Yuan Beef Noodle
places.note: Neighbourhood favourite with a rich braise and generous meat portions.

places.name: Liuhe Night Market
places.note: Late-night bowls when the sit-down shops have already closed.

food.name: Lu rou fan
food.desc: Minced or braised pork stewed with soy and five spice, ladled glossy over rice; the cheapest great meal in the city.

places.name: Bo Home braised pork rice
places.note: Michelin-listed old shop pairing braised pork rice with milkfish soup.

places.name: Ruifeng Night Market
places.note: Multiple stalls do rice bowls with braised pork and pickled greens.

food.name: Cijin seafood
food.desc: Grilled squid, salt-baked prawns and steamed crab straight off the boats on the sandbar island across the harbour.

places.name: Cijin Seafood Street
places.note: Pick your fish from the tanks; a short ferry ride from Gushan pier.

places.name: Cijin Old Street
places.note: Snack stalls for fried squid and papaya milk between seafood houses.

food.name: Night market snacks
food.desc: Oyster omelette, stinky tofu, salt-and-pepper chicken and grilled squid, worked through stall by stall after dark.

places.name: Ruifeng Night Market
places.note: The biggest and most local of Kaohsiung's markets; closed some weekdays.

places.name: Liuhe Night Market
places.note: Tourist-friendly and central, right by Formosa Boulevard station.

places.name: Ziqiang Night Market
places.note: Compact strip of food carts that regulars rate above the big markets.

food.name: Papaya milk
food.desc: Ripe papaya blended with fresh milk and ice into a thick, faintly floral shake, a southern Taiwan night market fixture.

places.name: Liuhe Night Market papaya milk stands
places.note: The market's best-known drink; several rival stalls sit side by side.

places.name: Ruifeng Night Market
places.note: Same shake, bigger cups, usually a shorter queue.

food.name: Winter melon tea and sugarcane juice
food.desc: Cooling caramel-sweet winter melon tea and freshly pressed sugarcane juice, sold from roadside stands all year in the tropical south.

places.name: Yancheng District drink stands
places.note: Old-town shops still boil their own winter melon sugar blocks.

places.name: Liuhe Night Market
places.note: Juice carts press sugarcane to order alongside the food stalls.

landmarks: Fo Guang Shan Buddha Museum
An awe-inspiring axis of eight pagodas leads to a 108-meter seated bronze Buddha, Taiwan's grandest Buddhist complex and pilgrimage magnet.
Lotus Pond (Dragon and Tiger Pagodas)
Enter through the dragon's mouth and exit the tiger's jaws at these whimsical twin pagodas, stars of a lake rimmed with temples.
Dome of Light (Formosa Boulevard MRT Station)
The world's largest one-piece glasswork blazes across a metro station ceiling, 4,500 panels telling a story of water, earth, light and fire.
Pier-2 Art Center
Abandoned harbor warehouses reborn as Taiwan's coolest arts district, packed with murals, installations, indie shops and waterfront railway relics.
Cijin Island
A five-minute ferry reaches this narrow harbor island of seafood streets, a 1883 lighthouse, black-sand beaches and sunset rainbow arches.
Love River (Ai He)
Kaohsiung's romantic waterway glitters with lit bridges and café terraces, best enjoyed from an evening gondola-style cruise boat.
Former British Consulate at Takao
An 1879 red-brick colonial residence on a bluff above Sizihwan Bay, pairing harbor-mouth sunset views with afternoon tea.
85 Sky Tower
The 348-meter tuba-shaped skyscraper that defines Kaohsiung's skyline, its upper floors surveying the harbor's cranes and container ballet.
Liuhe Night Market
The city's most famous night market grills papaya milk, seafood congee and sizzling squid along a pedestrianized downtown street.
Shoushan (Monkey Mountain) and Sizihwan Bay
Coastal trails busy with cheeky Formosan macaques climb above Sizihwan's beach, delivering green respite and Taiwan Strait sunsets.

train.note: Taiwan is an island with no international trains. High Speed Rail from Kaohsiung's Zuoying station races up the west coast to Tainan (~11 min), Taichung (~45 min) and Taipei (~1h45); conventional Taiwan Railways (TRA) trains from Kaohsiung Station also run the coast and the slower southern and eastern lines toward Kenting's gateway and Taitung.

bus.note: No international coaches run from Taiwan. Kuo-Kuang, UBus and other operators run frequent intercity highway coaches from the Kaohsiung bus stations to Tainan, Taichung, Chiayi and Taipei, plus buses south toward Kenting.

ferry.note: Kaohsiung's ferries are domestic. Frequent commuter ferries cross the harbor from Gushan to Cijin Island (~5 min) and run within the port, while seasonal passenger ferries sail from Kaohsiung out to the Penghu islands (Magong) in the Taiwan Strait.

half.name: Tainan
half.blurb: Taiwan's oldest city and former capital, packed with temples, Dutch-era forts and celebrated street food, about 40 minutes north by high-speed rail.

full.name: Kenting National Park
full.blurb: Taiwan's tropical southern tip of coral beaches, surf and national-park headlands, roughly two to three hours south by bus or car.

full.name: Alishan
full.blurb: A misty high-mountain forest of ancient cypress, seas of cloud at sunrise and a historic narrow-gauge railway, a long day trip inland.
